attribution.note: Zitron directly endorses the causal assertion.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the asserted policy sequence and effect on access clarity. The separate hedged judgment about a swindle is correctly excluded.

contract.note: Reduced ascertainability is an ordinary reading of the statement. Requiring comparative evidence distinguishes uncertainty about access from simply receiving less access.

evidence.note: Supports the temporary off-peak increase component. The advertised expiry does not establish increased uncertainty or an undisclosed reduction.

The March 26 announcement precedes the reported promotion expiry, challenging the asserted sequence. The company disclosure also gives an 11AM endpoint. Neither settles the causal effect on ascertainability.
An identifiable, unverified subscriber report documents uncertainty before the peak-hour announcement. It cannot isolate the effect of overlapping policy changes.

reviews.rationale: The promotion and peak-hour changes are documented, with counterevidence to their asserted order. No comparable before-and-after evidence establishes whether the changes made access harder to determine. The chronology discrepancy alone does not resolve the causal assertion.

attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses all three components about Anthropic and OpenAI.

semantics.note: The normalization changes failure at prices approaching sustainability into failure at sustainable prices. It should retain that pricing qualification and explicitly preserve the consumer and business scope.

contract.note: The commercial-usefulness reading is ordinary. The annual period and net-loss basis are evaluator choices, appropriately disclosed; losses alone cannot establish the stronger viability assertions.

evidence.note: Anthropic's audited company filing supports its 2025 multibillion-dollar net-loss component. Large financing revaluations must be distinguished from operating costs. It does not establish absence of a profitable route.

Reporting on audited statements supports OpenAI's 2025 multibillion-dollar reported net loss, while distinguishing restructuring charges. It supplies no matched evidence of customer economics at sustainable prices.

reviews.rationale: The historical loss components are corroborated on the disclosed reporting bases. Neither company's losses establish that no credible profitable route existed at publication. The packet lacks fully allocated costs, corresponding prices, and customer retention evidence needed to resolve the compound commercial claim.

attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts permanent inability to achieve profitability.

semantics.note: The statement firmly commits to never becoming profitable. Customer anger is supporting reasoning, not a conditional antecedent.

contract.note: Company-wide cost coverage is an ordinary business reading. Allowing a completed quarter and reconciled adjusted profitability fairly respects the breadth of the assertion; accounting details determine whether an event qualifies.

evidence.note: Reuters reports Anthropic's claim of adjusted Q3 profitability through attendees. This is material counterevidence, but the undefined adjustments do not establish recurring-cost coverage or satisfy the early-resolution rule.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. Reported adjusted profitability warrants consideration, but no reconciliation establishes a qualifying profitable period. No permanent cessation with complete lifetime records is documented either, so neither early-resolution condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron directly endorses the sector profitability assessment.

semantics.note: The surrounding discussion identifies GPU rental. The evidential framing is a firm assessment, not a probabilistic hedge or an explicit claim about every individual provider.

contract.note: Margins after depreciation and relevant financing costs fit the surrounding argument. Selecting 2025 from the adjacent example is reasonable. The contract appropriately avoids inventing a numerical threshold for low margins.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's filing discloses negative consolidated annual margins. These company-wide figures do not isolate GPU rental or establish a representative sector pattern.

The company discloses a positive quarterly adjusted operating margin. Its period, accounting basis, and consolidated scope differ from the sector assessment; a positive margin also need not contradict low margins.

reviews.rationale: The packet supplies one provider's consolidated losses and a quarterly adjusted positive margin. Neither establishes comparable GPU rental profitability across representative sector activity. The ordinary reading is assessable, but the available evidence does not settle it.
